results.text: The platform-wide database convention adopts PostgreSQL 16 as the database for every service datastore, with no exceptions unless an accepted Architecture Decision Record (ADR) authorizes one. SQLite is the ranked fallback and is permitted only for embedded tooling and local-development fixtures; it must never be used as a service datastore. MySQL is explicitly not used on the platform. The canonical PostgreSQL setup provisions databases through the platform Terraform modules using module "postgres", creates one PostgreSQL instance per service, prohibits shared databases between services, runs migrations with sqitch using migration files stored in the owning service's repository under "migrations/", and provides connection pooling through pgbouncer configured in transaction mode. This convention applies to all service datastores across the platform. Analytics workloads have no decided exception as of the convention date; any analytics-specific store requires its own accepted ADR. | When: Monday, July 20, 2026, the date of the convention; the convention is standing and ongoing | Involving: The platform and all services operating service datastores; platform Terraform modules; PostgreSQL 16; SQLite; MySQL; sqitch; pgbouncer; service owners responsible for their repositories; and the ADR approval process. Analytics workloads are also covered because they have no decided exception. | The platform standardizes on PostgreSQL 16 to provide one consistent database technology for every service datastore. SQLite is restricted to embedded tooling and local-development fixtures because those uses do not constitute service datastores. MySQL is an explicit anti-preference and may override the platform convention only when a vendor dependency cannot run against PostgreSQL and that exception is recorded in an accepted ADR. Any other exception, including an analytics-specific store, likewise requires its own accepted ADR. The canonical setup establishes service isolation through one instance per service with no shared databases, standardized infrastructure provisioning through the platform Terraform module named "postgres", reproducible migration management through sqitch with migrations kept in the owning service repository, and transaction-mode connection pooling through pgbouncer.

The canonical service-datastore architecture provisions infrastructure through the platform Terraform module named "postgres", creates one PostgreSQL instance per service, and prohibits shared databases between services.

The structured JSON document must be the source of truth for every report, and the HTML artifact must be derived from that JSON and reproducible from it. Every numeric metric stored in the JSON must include three pieces of information: its value, its unit, and a `source_ref` that points to the upstream fact from which the metric was computed. | When: The requirements were established with the decision on Saturday, August 15, 2026; they apply whenever a report is generated, stored, rendered, or regenerated | Involving: Report generators that calculate and write numeric metrics; upstream systems or facts referenced by `source_ref`; the publish-time HTML renderer; report readers; and maintainers of the `report.v2` schema | Making JSON authoritative prevents the stored data and its presentation from becoming competing sources of truth. Requiring `value`, `unit`, and `source_ref` preserves metric meaning, units, provenance, and traceability to the upstream fact used in the calculation. Reproducible HTML ensures that the presentation can be recreated from the authoritative JSON document.
